title: openai-compat: support Responses variants, seed/determinism & metadata passthrough
author: Amira Khan
description: Motivation: customers using the OpenAI Responses-style endpoints expect parity for newer features (seed/determinism flags, metadata passthrough, structured output variants) and more stable streaming behavior when using function/tool calling. This PR extends the OpenAI compatibility adapter to recognize Responses API variants, surface and persist the seed/determinism fields through the request/response lifecycle, and passthrough user-provided metadata into our event/audit logs and response envelope. Changes include adapter-level protocol updates, SDK surface tweaks, and end-to-end tests. The change is backwards-compatible: older OpenAI-style requests continue to be supported; when seed is not provided we keep existing sampling behavior. Checklist: - implement Responses variant routing and feature flags - thread seed/determinism through runtime kernel selection + cache keys - expose metadata passthrough in compatibility layer and persist to audit logs - add end-to-end tests including streaming+function-calling combos - update docs and SDK shims Implementation notes: we add a Responses adapter that normalizes incoming payloads into our internal request model, carrying an optional "seed" and a boolean "deterministic" flag. The adapter augments cache keys and sampling paths when seed/determinism are present to ensure deterministic outputs and cache partitioning. Metadata is attached to the request context and included in emitted events and the OpenAI-compat response "metadata" field for downstream customers. Streaming stability: we found a race when a streamed function call finished while structured-output parsing was still buffering; added a small ordering fence in stream finalization and a retry-safe parsing pass to avoid truncated JSON. Tests and CI: added unit tests for adapter normalization, integration tests across streaming + function-calling, and a deterministic regression test harness that runs with fixed seeds. Performance: trivial overhead in the adapter path; measured 0.6% median latency increase in the critical path and deterministic cache hits reduce repeated work for replayed seeds. Rollout: feature-flagged, staged rollout to 10% of traffic for 48h, monitoring for delta in token cost and regressions in eval sets. Docs: updated openai_compat.md and SDK shim docs. Migration: customers may opt-in to seed/determinism by passing the new fields; no change required for existing clients.

review_comments: Jonah Peters: Can you confirm cache key layout changes are backward compatible? Requested that seed be namespaced to avoid collisions with existing numeric user metadata.
Amira Khan: Reply: seed is namespaced under compat.seed in the cache key; added explicit tests to assert old keys remain resolvable.
Lena Ortiz: Please add an integration test for streaming + function-calling where function returns structured JSON larger than 8KB; previous bug truncated output.
Amira Khan: Reply: added test and a small ordering fence in streaming finalization to address this; CI flake reproduced locally and fixed.
Marcus Lee: Approve after CI green and docs updated. Left a minor nits suggestion for wording in the SDK doc examples.

release_notes: Added OpenAI Responses compatibility: seed/determinism flags supported; metadata passed through to audit/events and included in compatibility response; improved streaming stability for structured output and function calling. Backwards-compatible and feature-flagged rollout.
notes_on_ci: CI originally showed two flaky test failures related to streaming timeouts; reran determinism job and fixed ordering fence which stabilized tests. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, docs).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: deterministic seeds may change caching semantics and increase cache fragmentation; mitigation: namespaced cache keys and staged rollout with telemetry to detect cache miss rate changes. Rolling back feature flag immediately reverts behavior.
how_to_validate: 1) Run new e2e suite: pytest redwood/tests/test_streaming_function_calls.py 2) Smoke test with SDK: call Responses endpoint with seed and deterministic=true and confirm stable outputs across repeated calls 3) Verify metadata appears in telemetry/audit logs and in the /compat response envelope
